transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20 15:00 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood Solutions Eng), Priya Sharma (NectarWell Head of ML), Ethan Cole (CTO), Martine Lopez (Localization PM), Diego Alvarez (Platform Eng), Sana Iqbal (Data Scientist)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
NectarWell wants to run a 4-week POC to validate an open-model for triage and patient-facing Q&A in English + Spanish and Portuguese. Key constraints: must keep avg latency below 300ms for single-turn FAQ work, support bursts up to 2k qps for short spikes, maintain medical hallucination risk below X (see rubric), and ensure data residency/compliance compatibility. Redwood suggested a 3-model shortlist (small/med/large variants) and a bench plan with both latency and correctness evals. Action items and deadlines captured.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood, and with me are Lena and Jordan. is that sound okay on your end?
[00:07] Priya: yeah great, can hear you. thanks for setting this up. we wanted to make sure we put everything on the table — multilingual, clinical safety, and the practical infra costs.
[00:15] Ethan: hi, quick intro — i'm Ethan, CTO. main ask: can you help us pick a model for the POC that won't blow our ops cost but meets safety bar for triage answers.
[00:24] Lena: great, super helpful. before we dive into models, quick clarifying q: what's your primary load profile? steady vs spike?
[00:30] Diego: mostly steady ~200 qps weekdays but sudden marketing pushes create spikes to ~2k qps for a few minutes. we need elastic handling without huge overprovision.
[00:39] Samir: understood. POC baseline we'll plan for steady ~200 qps with burst test to 2k qps. what's the latency SLO you're targeting?
[00:44] Priya: for the triage/FAQ flow we want median <200ms and p95 <400ms ideally — but we can stretch p95 to 500ms during spike tests.
[00:52] Lena: ok noted. that pushes us toward quantized medium models or optimized kernels with prefix caching. also we should discuss safety metrics — how are you measuring hallucination tolerance?
[01:02] Priya: good question. we have an internal rubric — which i'll share — that scores factual alignment, presence of hallucinated entities, and risky recommendations. target: >92% on alignment tests on our gold set, and near-zero risky clinical advice.
[01:15] Sana: i'll attach the rubric and a small labeled set. there are items in Spanish and Portuguese too, roughly 15-20% of samples.
[01:24] Jordan: perfect — that helps a lot for bench design. for model shortlist, do you have brand constraints? are open-source models acceptable?
[01:32] Ethan: open-source is preferable. we want control for audit and potential private deployment.
[01:36] Samir: great, so we typically propose a three-tier shortlist: a smaller highly-optimized model for fast low-cost inference, a mid-size model that balances quality/cost, and a larger model for quality checks. for example — illustrative only — Llama-2-13B-q4 / Mistral-Instruct 7BQuant / Falcon-40B-pt-8k depending on your safety/perf needs.
[01:54] Martine: quick interrupt — some of those names are fuzzy in our docs, can you spell out expected multilingual competence please? we need decent Spanish/Portuguese.
[02:02] Lena: yes. smaller models will generally be weaker on non-English, especially Portuguese. mid models like Mistral variants often have surprisingly decent multilingual generalization if they've been instruction-tuned with multi-lingual data. large 40B class models give best raw coverage but at much higher cost and infra.
[02:20] Priya: what about domain adaptation — can we do light RL or instruction tuning on our dataset? we have 10k closed-case QA pairs we've labeled.
[02:28] Samir: for POC we recommend inference-time prompt engineering + few-shot examples and a light fine-tune or LoRA on the mid model if you want to push the quality quickly. full-fine-tune on large models is expensive.
[02:38] Diego: infrastructure question — can we run this in our VPC? we can't send PHI to hosted environments for the pilot.
[02:44] Jordan: we support Redwood Private (VPC) option. for initial bench runs, we can also provision a dedicated trial cluster in a compliant region with your network peering, we will share the network diagram and SOC2 docs.
[02:57] Ethan: good. costs — any ballpark on GPU hours for a 2k qps spike test if we use a 13B quantized model?
[03:04] Lena: estimates: for q4 quantized 13B optimized kernels, sustained 200 qps can be done on a small pool of A10s or equivalent with batching; burst to 2k qps needs autoscaling and more instances — rough pilot estimate ~8-12 GPU-hours for a multi-minute stress run; we'll give a more precise chart in the bench plan.
[03:22] Priya: ok that's manageable. next, quality metrics: beyond your rubric, we want BLEU/ROUGE? or prefer specialized medical information retrieval metrics?
[03:32] Samir: for triage and Q&A we combine: (1) exact match / semantic similarity to gold answers, (2) hallucination detection (entity-level mismatches), (3) safety classification (flagging risky recommendations). we can add retrieval-augmented evals to see if RAG+smaller model beats larger model.
[03:46] Sana: curious — how does RAG change cost dynamics? if we use vector DB plus a 7B model, is that cheaper than a 40B?
[03:53] Lena: often yes. RAG front-loads storage/CPU costs and lets smaller models answer reliably; it depends on your retrieval hit-rate and how often you need long-context synthesis. For short triage answers, RAG+7B is a compelling trade.
[04:06] Martine: for the multilingual samples, retrieval will need localized documents. we have Spanish/Portuguese KB pages but coverage is lower.
[04:14] Priya: we'll prioritize Spanish content for the bench.
[04:18] Samir: timeline suggestion: week 0 (this week) finalize shortlist + sample sets; week 1 run functional quality evals on 3 models; week 2 run latency + stress bench; week 3 iterate on light fine-tuning / RAG tweaks and produce POC report. does that align?
[04:33] Ethan: yes, that's tight but doable. we have internal resources to prep data in 3-4 business days.
[04:38] Diego: one more infra note — our platform requires SOC2 and SSO integration. what's typical lead time for SSO with Redwood Private?
[04:46] Jordan: SSO via SAML works — lead time depends on info exchange; for POC we can do token-based access for bench runs, and parallelize SSO setup; 2-week window is typical for full enterprise SSO.
[04:58] Priya: good. on the shortlist, can you be explicit about expected p50/p95 latencies for each model class under our 200 qps steady profile?
[05:06] Lena: rough numbers — 7B quantized on optimized kernels: p50 ~80-120ms, p95 ~200-350ms with batching; 13B q4: p50 ~140-220ms, p95 ~300-450ms; 40B (optimized / sparsified) p50 ~250-400ms, p95 ~600ms+. these are approximate, and depend on sequence length and batch config.
[05:28] Priya: sequence length — our average prompt is ~120 tokens, average completion 40 tokens. is that favorable?
[05:33] Lena: yes, that's relatively short which helps latency. kv-cache hit rate for multi-turn helps if you're doing chat flows.
[05:40] Samir: another tradeoff is quantization quality — q4 can introduce subtle hallucination behavior sometimes, we'll surface that in the bench.
[05:48] Martine: about evaluation — can Redwood run bilingual scoring (EN/ES/PT) automatically?
[05:53] Jordan: we'll adapt the bench harness to compute semantic similarity in multi-lingual embedding space and sample manual checks for safety-critical outputs. we'll include per-language breakdowns.
[06:04] Sana: will you also share the bench scripts so we can reproduce locally?
[06:08] Jordan: yes, we'll share a repo and runbook.
[06:11] Priya: outstanding items — what do we need to finalize today to start week 1?
[06:15] Samir: commitments: you share the 5k sample set + rubric; we share model shortlist + bench plan and cost envelope; agree on bench schedule and access mode (VPC or hosted trial).
[06:24] Ethan: we prefer VPC trial. Samir, can you confirm minimal network requirements?
[06:28] Samir: yes, we'll send a one-pager network whitelist and peering steps.
[06:31] Martine: one worry — data retention and audit logs. can we get per-request audit trails and token-level cost breakdowns?
[06:38] Jordan: yes on-console token breakdowns and per-request traces for Redwood Dedicated/Private. we'll add log retention options in the doc.
[06:45] Priya: any red flags re regulatory risk if we run pilot in-hosted region?
[06:49] Jordan: avoid hosted for PHI. the hosted API is fine for synthetic demos but for real patient data we strongly recommend Private with KMS and VPC.
[06:58] Samir: final recap: our immediate deliverables — model shortlist + bench plan (Samir/Lena), bench scripts + repo (Jordan), network + SOC docs (Jordan), dataset + rubric (Priya/Sana). Next meeting: schedule after bench plan is shared, likely 60m during week of 2026-01-26 to kick off runs.
[07:18] Ethan: sounds good. any other questions?
[07:21] Martine: just one — will the bench include a RAG variant?
[07:25] Lena: yes we'll run RAG+7B vs 13B vs 40B baseline and report cost/quality tradeoffs.
[07:31] Priya: great. thanks everyone.
[07:34] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and the calendar invite for the bench run.
[07:38] [call ends — rough auto-generated end]

Notes on transcript quality: there are several minor name transcriptions and model names may be spelled differently in sections; attendees filled in clarifications during the call.
